page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng benchmarks and high single-threaded compression and decompression speeds, with gzip compression reaching 37.39 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 16.63 GB/sec. However, due to its low core count, multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU scores, and Passmark database operations fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is average for large uncached blocks (45.68 GB/sec read, 26.65 GB/sec write) but weak for small cached blocks. LLM inference on a small 135M model achieves an average text generation speed of 164.6 tokens/sec, though prompt processing is weak at 377.93 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n4d-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring strong single-threaded execution without massive memory overhead. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for compute-heavy tasks that do not scale across multiple cores or require large memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include lightweight single-threaded processing, basic web serving (averaging 7.78 GB/sec throughput), and small-scale utility scripts. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded high-performance computing, or large-scale LLM inference.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 2 vCPUs and 4.0 GB of RAM, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core CPU execution, with high single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds. However, multi-core performance, database operations, and small-block memory bandwidth are weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Large-block memory bandwidth and static web serving throughput remain average. Qualitatively, this instance provides a cost-efficient profile for single-threaded tasks and lightweight compute workloads with low memory demands. It is best suited for basic web serving, single-threaded utility scripts, and lightweight applications that benefit from dedicated AMD EPYC single-core performance.
